title: MLB proposes a 154-game season and seven-game division series
dek: The offer came in labor talks with the players' union. The league ties all of it to a salary cap, which the union opposes.
what: Major League Baseball proposed cutting the regular season from 162 games to 154 in a bargaining session with the players' union, the MLBPA, on 8 October. ESPN's Jeff Passan reported it in a post on X. MLB's own account on X lists the same package.

CBS Sports reports the 154-game schedule and a best-of-seven division series would start in 2029. Higher seeds choosing their wild card and division series opponents would start in 2027. CBS also reports a weekly off-day in the plan.

CBS reports that MLB made every proposal contingent on the players agreeing to a salary cap. The union said the league "once again made clear that all of its proposals are contingent on players' agreement to a salary cap." It said players will weigh in and respond at the bargaining table.
CBS reports the current labor agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on 1 December 2026. I did not confirm that date in a primary document.
why: A shorter season changes every team's schedule and pay, and the offer is tied to the cap fight, so fans, players and owners each read it differently.
next: The union has said it will respond at the bargaining table. The current agreement runs out on 1 December, per CBS.
